transcript.text: Alright everyone, we're two weeks out from the first production customer launch of the event-ingestion service. Both the streaming and hourly batch architectures have passed the functional test suite in dev, and I'll be making the binding architecture decision today. Per our normal routine, I need to hear the final checks from application architecture and compliance before I record the operating plan. Whoever owns those reviews, please go ahead and share your final check, including any concrete configuration or control actions required for launch. I'll capture all of those in the operating plan once both checks are heard.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: During testing of an unrelated replay tool yesterday, I measured a launch-period burst of about 18,000 events per minute that the hourly batch design cannot process within the customer-facing latency target. The streaming design needs exactly 12 partitions for that load, and the launch plan must include provisioning those 12 partitions and validating replay capacity before launch. I have not yet updated the architecture document because the replay test was outside the launch checklist.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I confirmed with the privacy office this morning that the first customer's event payloads must remain in the EU and be retained for exactly 400 days for an audit requirement. The launch plan must include a data-residency control confirming that payloads remain in the EU. I had not added this to the launch review yet because the customer questionnaire was completed in a separate compliance system.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Provision exactly 12 partitions for the streaming architecture to handle the launch-period burst of approximately 18,000 events per minute.
Implement and confirm a data-residency control ensuring all customer event payloads remain in the EU.
Configure event payload retention to exactly 400 days to satisfy the audit requirement.
